one_liner: Senior all-source intelligence analyst at DFC who researches classified and unclassified threats, writes intelligence products, and briefs senior leaders on counterintelligence risks.
fit_summary: This posting is open to the public, but it requires a year of GS-12-level experience as a multi-source intelligence analyst with working knowledge of the intelligence community. Daniel's research (Rural Health Transformation Program tracking, a state agency's training review, contract opportunity research) is policy and market research, not intelligence analysis, so he is unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and federal transition candidates; a separate Merit Promotion announcement (27-SID-ST-13099059-CH) is for status candidates only.

Requires one year of specialized experience at the GS-12 level covering ALL three elements: multi-source intelligence analysis and production, advanced analytical methods applied to multiple sources, and working knowledge of the national intelligence community's structure and operations.
Education cannot substitute at GS-13; no degree is required.
The position requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access, which means a Top Secret background investigation and possibly a polygraph.
The application window is very short: October 29 to November 4, 2026.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year of GS-12-level multi-source intelligence analysis, and his research is policy and market research, not intelligence analysis.

More realistically, target GS-9/11 emergency management, program analyst, or legislative and policy roles at FEMA, DHS, Virginia VDEM or Prince William County, where his IEM and policy background fits directly.
resume_bullets: Provided scholarly research that helped a state public health agency's analysts review trauma-incident training recertification.
Studied Middle East ethnography and global trade for an M.A. in Global Affairs (George Mason, 2016).
interview_questions: Walk us through an analytic product you wrote: what sources did you use, and how did you communicate confidence and gaps?
How would you handle conflicting reporting from two credible sources?
Describe your understanding of the Intelligence Community's structure and how DFC might interact with it.
Tell us about briefing a senior leader who disagreed with your assessment.
watch_outs: The specialized experience is narrow (an intelligence-analyst background), and his resume doesn't show it.
SCI clearance processing is lengthy and may involve a polygraph.
The job is in-office in Washington, DC with telework eligibility, so expect a commute from Manassas.
